structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E001.

Measured: the airbench96-style port (9 epochs, eager, fp16 channels_last, GPU-resident data, label smoothing 0.3, no TTA) gave 3-seed accuracy 0.7430 at 9.43 s. That is about 1 pp below the 0.753 bar. Both numbers fell inside my ranges and near my points (10.8 s, 0.746), so my priors survive with small updates.

Time budget, per what E001 implies:
- Fixed cost (uint8 transfer, normalisation, whitening eigh on 5k images, pad, flip mask) is roughly 0.2-0.4 s, about 3-4% of the run. H3 and H3.2 are small levers. The tip already drops the ragged batch (steps = n//bs), so I006 has almost nothing to remove unless compile adds new shapes.
- Per-epoch cost is about 1.0 s eager. Most of it is GPU compute in conv/BN/GELU. The rest is unfused BN and GELU elementwise traffic and some launch overhead under the 4-CPU pin. torch.SGD already uses foreach on CUDA, so a fused optimizer gains little. Compiling (fusing BN+GELU, the residual add and the pool) should cut about 8-15% per epoch, giving roughly 8.2-8.7 s at 9 epochs. Progressive resizing at 24/28/32 px cuts FLOPs to about 75%, but fixed overhead doesn't scale down, so it saves about 15-20% of time.

Accuracy budget:
- The deficit is about 1 pp. My slope estimate near 9 epochs is about +0.5-0.7 pp per epoch at about +11% time. Reaching 0.756 (the 40-seed-safe margin) from 0.743 by epochs alone would take about 11 epochs, roughly 11.3 s eager, or about 10 s compiled.
- Cheaper accuracy sources should be bought before epochs. EMA/Lookahead (+0.1-0.3 pp at about 1-2% time) is one. Width or label-smoothing tuning is another. Any lever that costs accuracy (progressive resizing, Muon with transferred CIFAR-10 hyperparameters, bigger batches) has to repay that accuracy in epochs. At about 11% time per 0.6 pp, a 15% time saving that costs more than about 0.8 pp is a net loss.
- Order of gains: compile (pure time saving) > EMA (cheap accuracy) > epochs (the dial) > resizing/Muon (uncertain net).

Noise: I assume per-seed std of about 0.2-0.35 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.15-0.2 pp, and run-to-run time drift of about 1-2%. Effects under 0.3 pp are not resolvable in one 3-seed run.

Unsure about:
- the true epoch slope (could be 0.3 or 1.0 pp per epoch);
- how much of the 1 s/epoch is CPU-launch-bound. If a lot, compile and CUDA graphs gain more than 15%;
- whether Muon's sample efficiency survives the CIFAR-100 transfer at batch 2000.

forecasts.reason: The port is below the bar, so this runs 9→10 epochs. That is about +11% time and +0.4-0.8 pp, which maps to about +5.5% and +0.2-0.4 pp per half-epoch, inside H4.2.1's band. Weak vote.
Fusing BN+GELU and the residual trims about 10-15% of the eager per-epoch cost. torch.SGD is already foreach, so the optimizer swap adds little. A borderline 10% result is possible.
An expected gain of 0.1-0.3 pp is comparable to the 3-seed SE of about 0.2 pp. Time cost is about 1-3%.
An identical rerun should drift under 2% in time, and per-seed std should land around 0.2-0.35 pp.
The tip already drops the ragged batch (n//bs steps), so there is no shape to save. A gain of 0.3 s or more is unlikely.

Batch 2000 halves the step count. The hyperparameters were tuned on CIFAR-10, and Newton-Schulz on 576-wide filters adds cost. It probably doesn't beat SGD's accuracy at the same epochs, let alone with fewer.
Compute falls to about 75% of FLOPs, saving about 15% of time, but expected accuracy loss is 0.5-1 pp. That far exceeds the 0.2 pp allowance, and recovering it costs about 1 epoch.

cruxes: How many pp of accuracy does each extra epoch buy near 9-11 epochs? This sets the time price of the ~1.3 pp still needed (0.743 to about 0.756).
What fraction of the ~1.0 s/epoch eager cost is CPU launch or elementwise overhead that compile or CUDA graphs can remove? Is it 10% or 30%?
Are there accuracy sources cheaper than epochs, such as EMA, width or label-smoothing retuning, or Muon, that add 0.5 pp or more at under 5% time?
